\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{भाकीत} (bhākīt)}{भाकीत (bhākīt)}]{\mr{भाकीत} (bhākīt) — a prediction; a forecast}

\label{lesson:MR-C383-bhakit}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for certain, then the Marathi for to seem.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{भाकीत}}
\textbf{\mr{भाकीत}} — \emph{bhākīt} — \textquotedblleft{}a prediction; a forecast\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{हवामान} \mr{खात्याने} \mr{पावसाचं} \mr{भाकीत} \mr{केलं}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{havāmān khātyāne pāvsācaṁ bhākīt kelaṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather department forecast rain.
\end{quote}

Neuter.

\mr{भाकीत} \mr{करणे}, to predict; \mr{भाकीत} \mr{खरं} \mr{होणे}, to come true.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{भाकीत}} (\emph{bhākīt}) is a Marathi noun whose origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhākīt}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhākīt}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{havāmān khātyāne pāvsācaṁ bhākīt kelaṁ.} — The weather department forecast rain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for certain, then the Marathi for to seem, then say \emph{bhākīt} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mr{भाकीत} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A prediction; a forecast\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{गृहीत} \mr{धरणे} (gṛhīt dharṇe)}{गृहीत धरणे (gṛhīt dharṇe)}]{\mr{गृहीत} \mr{धरणे} (gṛhīt dharṇe) — to assume; to take for granted}

\label{lesson:MR-C383-grhit-dharne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to seem, then the Marathi for a prediction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{गृहीत} \mr{धरणे}}
\textbf{\mr{गृहीत} \mr{धरणे}} — \emph{gṛhīt dharṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to assume; to take for granted\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{तू} \mr{येणार} \mr{नाहीस} \mr{असं} \mr{मी} \mr{गृहीत} \mr{धरलं}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tū yeṇār nāhīs asaṁ mī gṛhīt dharlaṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I assumed that you were not coming.
\end{quote}

Past, with -\mr{ने} (he …): \mr{त्याने} \mr{गृहीत} \mr{धरलं}, \emph{tyāne gṛhīt dharlaṁ}.

Also of people: \mr{कोणालाही} \mr{गृहीत} \mr{धरणे}, to take someone for granted.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{गृहीत} \mr{धरणे}} (\emph{gṛhīt dharṇe}) joins the tatsama \mr{गृहीत}, Sanskrit \emph{gṛhīta}, \textquotedblleft{}seized, taken, accepted\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), to \mr{धरणे}, \textquotedblleft{}to hold\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gṛhīt dharṇe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gṛhīt dharṇe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tū yeṇār nāhīs asaṁ mī gṛhīt dharlaṁ.} — I assumed that you were not coming.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for to seem, then the Marathi for a prediction, then say \emph{gṛhīt dharṇe} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{अपेक्षा} (apekṣā)}{अपेक्षा (apekṣā)}]{\mr{अपेक्षा} (apekṣā) — an expectation}

\label{lesson:MR-C383-apeksa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for a prediction, then the Marathi for to assume.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{अपेक्षा}}
\textbf{\mr{अपेक्षा}} — \emph{apekṣā} — \textquotedblleft{}an expectation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{आईवडिलांच्या} \mr{माझ्याकडून} \mr{खूप} \mr{अपेक्षा} \mr{आहेत}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āīvḍilāñcyā mājhyākaḍūn khūp apekṣā āhet.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My parents have high expectations of me.
\end{quote}

Feminine. Plural: \mr{अपेक्षा}, \emph{apekṣā}.

X \mr{कडून} \mr{अपेक्षा}, expectations of X; \mr{अपेक्षा} \mr{करणे}, to expect.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{अपेक्षा}} (\emph{apekṣā}) is a tatsama, taken from Sanskrit \emph{apekṣā}, \textquotedblleft{}looking round; expectation\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{apekṣā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{apekṣā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āīvḍilāñcyā mājhyākaḍūn khūp apekṣā āhet.} — My parents have high expectations of me.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for a prediction, then the Marathi for to assume, then say \emph{apekṣā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{कल} (kal)}{कल (kal)}]{\mr{कल} (kal) — a trend; an inclination}

\label{lesson:MR-C383-kal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to assume, then the Marathi for an expectation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{कल}}
\textbf{\mr{कल}} — \emph{kal} — \textquotedblleft{}a trend; an inclination\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{तरुणांचा} \mr{कल} \mr{शहरांकडे} \mr{आहे}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taruṇāñcā kal śahrāṅkaḍe āhe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Young people are inclined towards the cities.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

X \mr{कडे} \mr{कल} \mr{असणे}, to lean towards X.

\textbf{\mr{कल}} (\emph{kal}) is a Marathi noun whose origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{ताडणे} (tāḍṇe)}{ताडणे (tāḍṇe)}]{\mr{ताडणे} (tāḍṇe) — to size up; to guess rightly}

\label{lesson:MR-C383-tadne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for an expectation, then the Marathi for a trend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{ताडणे}}
\textbf{\mr{ताडणे}} — \emph{tāḍṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to size up; to guess rightly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{तो} \mr{खोटं} \mr{बोलत} \mr{आहे} \mr{हे} \mr{आईने} \mr{लगेच} \mr{ताडलं}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{to khoṭaṁ bolat āhe he āīne lagec tāḍlaṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mother saw at once that he was lying.
\end{quote}

Past, with -\mr{ने} (he …): \mr{त्याने} \mr{ताडलं}, \emph{tyāne tāḍlaṁ}.

Transitive: what is guessed is the object; \mr{हे} \mr{ताडलं}, guessed this.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{ताडणे}} (\emph{tāḍṇe}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Marathi \emph{tāḍṇẽ}, \textquotedblleft{}to investigate, discover, infer\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*taḍati}, \textquotedblleft{}stretches\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5633).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for an expectation, then the Marathi for a trend, then say \emph{tāḍṇe} again
\end{itemize}
